rows.name: horizontal turret speed setter (entity, float): control[i]+0x8
rows.method: twin rule: in the old build the horizontal setter is the vertical one 0xF0 later, byte-identical except RIP/call displacements (-0xF0, same targets), field +0xC -> +0x8 (2 bytes) and hash 0x9d5d6cc7 -> 0xcc0b45e5 (tools/horizontal.py asserts this on the old image). The same transformation of the new vertical body gives the expected new horizontal body at 0x105cf00 + 0xF0. Only its first 16 bytes are readable in any capture (page 0x105d000 is still encrypted in evidence/game-26088801.dll and in the live text dumps); all 16 match. The port therefore uses the WHOLE predicted body as this setter's signature: aim_data.bind_natives reads it with ReadProcessMemory and refuses (Unsupported native sentry setter) unless all 232 bytes match, before any call.
rows.role: write (native): turret horizontal speed - RUNTIME-GATED by the full-body signature
rows.live_check: L9: read 232 bytes at game+0x105cff0 once resident; must equal the predicted body
rows.runtime_gate: full 232-byte body compared by the mod before its first call; otherwise the mod refuses to bind

rows.name: BehaviorComponent behavior ids of the sentry profiles (Gatling, Machine gun, Laser cannon, Rocket, Flamethrower, Mortar, EMS mortar)
rows.method: behavior update dispatcher switch (old 0x472f60 table 0x4795c4 / new 0x479ca0 table 0x4802c4, 693 cases, case = id - 1). (1) Case shape signatures (tools/behavior_enum.py from the Laser Sentry Cooldown port): 207 -> 208 and 308 -> 309 are unique; Gatling and MG share one shape that exists exactly twice in each build (old 213, 312 / new 214, 313); every unique anchor between ids 135 and 457 has shift +1 and between 588 and 693 shift 0. (2) Code layout (tools/behavior_layout.py): every direct call of the case and of each state handler must land at the old callee plus the local code shift measured from uniquely migrated neighbours (or the callee's own unique window); exactly one candidate passes for each id: 213 -> 214 (12/12 calls; the twin 313 fails, its handlers sit where old 312's moved), 312 -> 313, 308 -> 309 (13/13), 319 -> 320, 323 -> 324, 611 -> 611 (one behavior-specific callee each at the exact local shift, the unshifted alternative fails); 207 -> 208: all 10 callees move by one uniform +0x6bd0, unique shape match. (3) State switches of 213/312/308/207 and their new cases are identical in shape, state count (12/12/13/12) and handler order. The ids themselves come from game data (settings lookup, code identical), so a wrong id would only stop at "Unsupported sentry behavior" before any write
rows.role: gate (behavior id per profile; mismatch fails closed)
rows.live_check: L6: behavior +0 of a deployed Gatling = 214, MG = 313 (others as mapped)
